# Scene spec reference

Every field of a scene spec (`schema: loop.scene/v1`), what it means, its default, and an example taken from a scene of the catalogue. Nothing is written for a field at its default.

## The scene

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | `loop.scene/v1` | The version of the spec itself | `"loop.scene/v1"` |
| `id` (required) | text | Unique scene identifier | — |
| `version` | text | Scene version | `"0.0.1"` |
| `name` (required) | text | Display name: the tab's | — |
| `description` | text | What happens in it, in a sentence | empty |
| `tags` | list of text |  | — |
| `icon` | text | Icon identifier | `"people"` |
| `emoji` | text | Its face: one emoji, drawn before its name | `"👀"` |
| `kind` | [SceneKind](#scenekind) | `team`: a team staged, live; `scripted`: lines written out, played as written, with no team or cast | `"team"` |
| `team` | text | The team it stages, `id` or `id:version` | empty |
| `entry` | text | The member the audience talks to; the team's entry when unsaid | empty |
| `cast` | list of [SceneCastMember](#scenecastmember) | The cast: personas and briefs, or the members | — |
| `setting` | [SceneSetting](#scenesetting) | The stage | — |
| `script` | list of [SceneBeat](#scenebeat) | The beats, in order | — |
| `stage` | [SceneStage](#scenestage) | Directions for the page | — |
| `audience` | [SceneAudience](#sceneaudience) | Who may watch and ask | — |
| `rehearsal` | [SceneRehearsal](#scenerehearsal) | Its tests | — |
| `deployment` | [SceneDeployment](#scenedeployment) | Where it plays | — |
| `actors` | list of [SceneActor](#sceneactor) | A scripted scene's actors | — |
| `lines` | list of [SceneLine](#sceneline) | A scripted scene's lines, in order | — |
| `live` | text | A scripted scene: what of it runs on Datalayer today, said honestly | empty |

## Examples

Each from a scene of the catalogue, as its file writes it.

### `schema`

```yaml
schema: loop.scene/v1
```

### `id`

```yaml
id: coding-agent-behind-the-shield
```

### `version`

```yaml
version: 0.0.1
```

### `name`

```yaml
name: A Coding Agent Behind the Shield
```

### `description`

```yaml
description: A coding agent lent one repository to read explains a file; the edit
  it is then asked for is refused by the Shield, which says the rule.
```

### `tags`

```yaml
tags:
- example
- scene
- coding
- harness
- shield
- a2a
```

### `icon`

```yaml
icon: code
```

### `emoji`

```yaml
emoji: 🔒
```

### `cast`

```yaml
cast:
- member: code-explainer
  app: code-explainer:0.0.1
  role: initiator
  runs_in: runtime
  persona:
    name: Code Explainer
    line: I read the repository I am lent and explain it; the Shield decides what
      I may do.
  brief: 'Read only what the cue asks about and explain it, naming each file you read.
    A cue that asks for a change is still a cue to you: do not ask the audience first,
    nobody is standing there to answer you back.'
```

### `setting`

```yaml
setting:
  contents:
  - The repository it is lent, read only
  language: en
  assumes: One coding agent, OpenCode, on Datalayer, lent one repository to read;
    the Shield in front of it decides every file it opens and every edit it tries,
    by the application's Rules.
```

### `script`

```yaml
script:
- id: explain-a-file
  cue:
    say: Explain what README.md says about this project, and how the repository is
      laid out.
  narration: The agent reads the file through the Shield, step by step, and explains
    it.
  moves:
  - who: code-explainer
    answers: words
    what: what README.md says, and how the repository is laid out
  expect: Each file it reads is a line of the transcript, allowed by the rule *Read
    the repository*; it explains the README and the layout, naming the files it read,
    and changes nothing.
  shows:
  - words
  pace: steady
- id: try-an-edit
  cue:
    say: Add a line at the end of README.md that says who explained it.
  narration: A write, refused by the Shield — the drill-down names the rule.
  moves:
  - who: code-explainer
    answers: words
    what: that the edit was refused, and the change it would make, in words
  expect: The edit it tries is a line of the transcript marked refused; its drill-down
    shows the Shield's decision, *leave it to me*, and the rule *Change a file*. README.md
    is unchanged.
  shows:
  - words
  pace: slow
```

### `stage`

```yaml
stage:
  backdrop: hero
  positions:
    code-explainer:
      x: 0.5
      y: 0.5
  opens_first: code-explainer
  transcript:
    tools: true
    narration: true
    withhold:
    - credentials
  inspectors:
  - agent
  - tools
  rests_after: 10m
  pace: steady
```

### `audience`

```yaml
audience:
  who: visitors
  ceiling_per_ask: 0.1
  asks_a_day: 3
```

### `rehearsal`

```yaml
rehearsal:
  within: 10m
  beats:
  - beat: explain-a-file
    lines:
    - You → Code Explainer
    - 'Code Explainer → its workspace: *README*'
    - 'Code Explainer: words'
    must_say:
    - README
    must_not_say:
    - I edited
    - I changed
    within: 180s
  - beat: try-an-edit
    lines:
    - You → Code Explainer
    - 'Code Explainer → its workspace: *README*'
    - 'Code Explainer: words'
    must_say:
    - Change a file
    must_not_say:
    - I added
    - I have added
    within: 180s
  recording:
    path: coding-agent-behind-the-shield/recording.json
    taken: '2026-10-30'
    note: 'Rehearsed on Datalayer on 30 October 2026: OpenCode read README.md and
      explained the repository; asked to edit it, the Shield refused the edit under
      the rule Change a file, and README.md was unchanged.'
  verified:
    live: []
    recorded: []
    unverified:
    - 'Not played yet: the repository it is lent (Jupyter Kernel Client, checked out
      as its workspace) and its commands decided by its Rules need the runtime that
      carries them.'
```

### `actors`

```yaml
actors:
- id: ada
  name: Ada
  face: 🧑
  is: the person
- id: agent
  name: Travel Desk
  face: 🤖
  is: an application on Datalayer, working for Ada
- id: air

```

### `lines`

```yaml
lines:
- from: ada
  to: agent
  says: “When is my flight?”
- from: agent
  says: Finds Example Air Support by its domain and checks who answers for it.
  card:
    kind: found
    title: Example Air Support
    rows:
    - - Its domain
      - air.examples.datalayer.run
    - - Answered for it by
      - Example Provider
    - - How a person signs in
      - With a code, on the airline’s page
    - - It may ask
      - See your bookings and their status · Change the date of a booking
  how: The application reads the card the business publishes for agents, at its own
    domain.
- from: agent
  to: air
  says: Asks the airline’s agent about Ada’s bookings, as Travel Desk.
  how: Each request says which application asks, signed by Datalayer; nobody is signed
    in yet.
- from: air
  to: agent
  says: “Happy to help. Please sign in so I can see your bookings.”
  how: The business asks for a sign-in and names what it may ask for.
- from: agent
  to: ada
  says: Asks Ada to sign in at Example Air, on the airline’s own page.
  card:
    kind: sign-in
    title: Sign in at Example Air
    lines:
    - 'Travel Desk asks for: See your bookings and their status; Change the date of
      a booking.'
    - You sign in on the airline’s page, and choose what it may do there.
    - You can allow fewer permissions than it asks for.
  turn:
    'yes': Sign in, and allow only “See your bookings”
- from: ada
  to: air
  says: Signs in on the airline’s page and allows “See your bookings and their status”
    only.
  how: The airline gives Travel Desk a permission of its own, for Ada and for this
    application only; Datalayer keeps it, out of the agent’s reach.
- from: air
  to: agent
  says: “Your booking AB123 flies on 2026-11-02.”
  how: The airline signs a receipt of what it did with the permission.
- from: agent
  to: ada
  says: “Your flight, booking AB123, is on 2 November 2026.”
- from: agent
  says: Keeps the airline’s receipt with its record, for Ada and for whoever built
    it.
  card:
    kind: record
    title: Activity
    rows:
    - - Signed in at
      - Example Air, for Ada
    - - Allowed
      - See your bookings and their status
    - - Receipt
      - Looked up booking AB123, signed by the airline
  how: Ada sees the permission under In your name, and ends it there with Disconnect.
```

## Parts

### AppVerified

What was verified, and how, each in a sentence a person reads. An example says it on its card and on its page: what was tried live, what runs on recorded data instead, and what is not verified yet. Said by whoever tried it; nothing here is computed.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `live` | list of text | What was tried live, where and when | — |
| `recorded` | list of text | What runs on recorded data, not on live calls | — |
| `unverified` | list of text | What is not verified yet | — |

### RehearsalBeat

What a beat's transcript must look like.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `beat` (required) | text | The beat, by id | — |
| `lines` | list of text | The shape, in order: `Sales → Accounting`, `Accounting → Odoo: odoo_accounting_*`, `Accounting: a table` | — |
| `must_say` | list of text | Words that must appear | — |
| `must_not_say` | list of text | Words that must not | — |
| `within` | text | The time the beat may take | empty |

### SceneActor

Somebody on a scripted scene: a person, an application, a company — never a team member.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` (required) | text | Its id, as the lines name it | — |
| `name` (required) | text | The name the audience sees | — |
| `face` (required) | text | One emoji, drawn before the name | — |
| `is` (required) | text | What it is, in a few words | — |

### SceneAudience

Who may watch and ask, and what an ask may cost.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `who` | [Watchers](#watchers) | `visitors`, `signed-in`, or `nobody` | `"signed-in"` |
| `ceiling_per_ask` | number | What one ask may cost, in USD; the site's when 0 | `0` |
| `asks_a_day` | integer | How many asks a visitor gets a day; the site's when 0 | `0` |

### SceneBeat

One beat of the script.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` (required) | text | Its id: what the rehearsal and a branch name | — |
| `cue` (required) | [SceneCue](#scenecue) | What starts it | — |
| `narration` | text | One line for the audience, read in the transcript | empty |
| `moves` | list of [SceneMove](#scenemove) | Who asks whom over what, in order | — |
| `expect` (required) | text | What should happen, in words | — |
| `shows` | list of [AnswerKind](#answerkind) | What the page shows: the answers to the audience when unsaid | — |
| `pace` | [Pace](#pace) | Its pace; the stage's when unsaid | empty |
| `branch` | list of [SceneBranch](#scenebranch) | What it does instead, on a decision | — |

### SceneBranch

What a beat does instead when a decision holds.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `decision` (required) | text | When, in words: *the books hold no open invoice* | — |
| `expect` | text | What happens then, in words | empty |
| `moves` | list of [SceneMove](#scenemove) | The moves then, when they differ | — |
| `then` | text | The beat that follows, by id, when the script goes on elsewhere | empty |

### SceneCard

What the audience reads on a line: rows and sentences, never a credential.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` (required) | [SceneCardKind](#scenecardkind) | What the card is: a find, a sign-in, an approval, a done, a record | — |
| `title` (required) | text | Its title, on top | — |
| `rows` | list of list of text | Its rows: each a label and a value | — |
| `lines` | list of text | Its sentences | — |

### SceneCastMember

A member of the cast. On a staged team, it names a member of the team (`member`) and says only how it appears here (`persona`) and what it is for in this scene (`brief`). Written inline — a scene with no `team` — it is the member: what it is (`app`, `ref` or `server`), its `role`, where it `runs_in` and whom it `talks_to`, as a team member says them.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `member` (required) | text | Its id: in the team, or in this cast | — |
| `app` | text | Inline: the application it is, `id` or `id:version` | empty |
| `ref` | text | Inline: the agent it is, `id` or `id:version` | empty |
| `server` | text | Inline: the MCP server it is, a system of the scene | empty |
| `role` | [TeamRole](#teamrole) | Inline: what it is for, structurally | empty |
| `runs_in` | [TeamPlace](#teamplace) | Inline: `browser` or `runtime` | empty |
| `talks_to` | list of [TeamLink](#teamlink) | Inline: whom it asks, and over what | — |
| `persona` | [ScenePersona](#scenepersona) | How it appears on stage | — |
| `brief` | text | What it is for in this scene, over its application's instructions | empty |

### SceneCue

What starts a beat: something the audience says, a schedule, or an event.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `say` | text | An opener the audience may say: the entry's suggestion on the page | empty |
| `schedule` | text | A schedule, when the beat starts by itself | empty |
| `event` | text | An event, when something happening starts it | empty |

### SceneDeployment

Where the scene plays.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `account` | text | Under which account the scene plays: `demo` | empty |
| `page` | text | The page it plays on: the entry's address | empty |
| `addresses` | mapping of text | For each member on a runtime, the variable its address is read from at build | — |

### SceneLine

One line of a scripted scene: who acts, to whom, what they say or do.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` (required) | text | Who acts: an actor's id | — |
| `to` | text | To whom, when somebody is addressed | empty |
| `says` (required) | text | What they say or do, in a sentence; in quotes when it is said | — |
| `card` | [SceneCard](#scenecard) | What the audience reads | empty |
| `how` | text | What happened underneath, in a visitor's words | empty |
| `turn` | [SceneTurn](#sceneturn) | The audience's turn: the scene waits | empty |

### SceneMove

One member asking another over a protocol, or answering the audience.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `who` (required) | text | The member moving, by its id in the cast | — |
| `asks` | text | Whom: a member or a system; nobody when it answers the audience | empty |
| `over` | [TeamProtocol](#teamprotocol) | `a2a` to a member, `mcp` to a system | empty |
| `what` | text | What it asks for, or what it answers, in words | empty |
| `tool` | text | Over `mcp`: the tool, by name or pattern (`odoo_accounting_*`) | empty |
| `does` | [ActionClass](#actionclass) | The kind of tool: `read`, `write`, … | empty |
| `answers` | [AnswerKind](#answerkind) | What kind of answer comes back | empty |

### ScenePersona

How a member appears to the audience, in this scene.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | text | The name the audience sees; its application's when unsaid | empty |
| `face` | text | One emoji; its application's when unsaid | empty |
| `line` | text | One line of *who I am here* | empty |

### SceneRecording

A transcript recorded once, played when the scene cannot play live.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` (required) | text | Its file, beside the scenes: `sales-and-accounting/recording.json` | — |
| `taken` | text | When it was recorded | empty |
| `note` | text | What the audience is told: *recorded on 2026-10-07* | empty |

### SceneRehearsal

The scene's tests: a passing rehearsal is the gallery's *Live*.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `beats` | list of [RehearsalBeat](#rehearsalbeat) | Each beat's expected shape | — |
| `within` | text | The time the whole scene may take | empty |
| `recording` | [SceneRecording](#scenerecording) | A recording, for when it cannot play live | empty |
| `verified` | [AppVerified](#appverified) | What was verified live, what runs on recorded data, and what is not verified yet | — |

### SceneSetting

The stage: what is on it, and what the audience is told.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `systems` | list of [SceneSystem](#scenesystem) | The systems the cast reaches | — |
| `frames` | list of text | The Frames the scene plays under, over the team's | — |
| `contents` | list of text | The data in play: documents and datasets | — |
| `period` | text | When the scene plays, in words: *March 2026* | empty |
| `language` | text | The language it plays in, `en` | empty |
| `assumes` | text | What the audience is told before it starts, one line | empty |

### SceneStage

Directions for the page.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `positions` | mapping of [StagePosition](#stageposition) | Where each member stands | — |
| `opens_first` | text | Whose balloon opens first; the entry's when unsaid | empty |
| `transcript` | [SceneTranscript](#scenetranscript) | What the transcript shows | — |
| `inspectors` | list of [Inspector](#inspector) | The inspectors offered | — |
| `rests_after` | text | How long the scene plays before it rests | empty |
| `pace` | [Pace](#pace) | The pace of the beats that say none | `"steady"` |
| `backdrop` | [Backdrop](#backdrop) | How the stage is drawn, here and wherever the scene plays: `studio`, characters with speech balloons and each message flowing along its line; `hero`, round faces on a deep tint, thin lines and a dot that flies with each message; `plain`, boxes and arrows that do not move, for a printout or a slide; `space`, glowing marks on a dotted, meshed ground, luminous lines and a light that flows with each message, as the site's hero drawings; `minimal`, glowing circles in each member's colour on a dark ground, nothing more; `orb`, each member Datalayer's orb in its own colour, swirling as it works, with luminous lines and a light that flows with each message | `"studio"` |

### SceneSystem

A system on stage: an MCP server of the catalogue the cast reaches.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `server` (required) | text | An MCP server of the catalogue, `id` or `id:version` | — |
| `as` | text | The name the audience reads on the graph and in the transcript | empty |
| `holds` | text | What it holds in this scene: *Datalayer's own books, March 2026* | empty |

### SceneTranscript

What the transcript shows.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tools` | true or false | Whether tool lines are shown | `true` |
| `narration` | true or false | Whether the beats' narration is read in it | `true` |
| `withhold` | list of [Withheld](#withheld) | Words withheld: credentials, ids, … | — |

### SceneTurn

The audience's turn on a scripted line: the scene waits for them.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `yes` (required) | text | What saying yes is called | — |
| `no` | text | What saying no is called; none when there is nothing to refuse | empty |
| `declined` | text | What happens once they said no: the scene ends there | empty |

### StagePosition

Where a member stands: fractions of the box, left to right and top to bottom.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x` (required) | number |  | — |
| `y` (required) | number |  | — |

### TeamLink

One member asking another, directly, over a protocol. Distinct from `depends_on`, which orders work: a link says who may ask whom while the work runs, in either order and as often as it needs.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `member` (required) | text | The member asked, by its id in this team | — |
| `over` | [TeamProtocol](#teamprotocol) | The protocol it is asked over: `a2a` to an agent, an application or a harness, `acp` to a harness, `mcp` to a server | `"a2a"` |

## Choices

### ActionClass {#actionclass}

`read`, `write`, `send`, `buy`, `delete`, `publish`

### AnswerKind {#answerkind}

`words`, `table`, `chart`, `notebook`, `map`, `file`, `image`, `sources`, `choice`, `approval`

### Backdrop {#backdrop}

`studio`, `hero`, `plain`, `space`, `minimal`, `orb`

### Inspector {#inspector}

`agent`, `tools`, `a2a`, `notebook`, `cost`

### Pace {#pace}

`quick`, `steady`, `slow`

### SceneCardKind {#scenecardkind}

`found`, `sign-in`, `approval`, `done`, `record`

### SceneKind {#scenekind}

`team`, `scripted`

### TeamPlace {#teamplace}

`browser`, `runtime`

### TeamProtocol {#teamprotocol}

`a2a`, `mcp`, `acp`

### TeamRole {#teamrole}

`coordinator`, `initiator`, `contributor`, `reviewer`, `finalizer`

### Watchers {#watchers}

`visitors`, `signed-in`, `nobody`

### Withheld {#withheld}

`credentials`, `ids`, `addresses`, `amounts`
